contracts.invariant: test-fn=false selects C identity index; a Scheme test/hash selects persistent SCHEME_INDEX bit 128. Same existing flags word; never infer ownership from KEY_MOVED or weak-key bits.
contracts.benefit: Native layout records the semantic algorithm owner before collector sees a table
contracts.cost: One constructor flag decision; no extra table field or root word

contracts.route: mem.c scan -> process_gc_hash_tables -> repaired key/value references and owner dispatch
contracts.invariant: Collector transports references. Scheme hashes must be stable for unchanged semantic keys across GC. Clear only address-driven KEY_MOVED for Scheme indexes; preserve pre-existing NEED_REHASH. Never call Scheme from GC or replace its index with the C address hash.
contracts.benefit: Eliminate wrong C rehash and its full-table traversal for Scheme-owned indexes; avoid adding a first-reader mutation after ordinary GC
contracts.cost: One owner branch per reached GC table. Correctness depends on hash stability; arbitrary physical-address-dependent custom hashes are not qualified.

contracts.route: Native identity tables and union/find -> existing eager SMP rehasher
contracts.invariant: Physical-address indexes rehash with the native algorithm after movement. New owner branch does not globally disable eager reconstruction.
contracts.benefit: Preserve existing C identity lookup and shared-read preparation
contracts.cost: Existing native rehash work retained; concurrent mutation and raw misuse remain separate contracts

contracts.route: _system.scm table-access -> recorded test/hash -> existing resize/reinsert for explicit reconstruction debt
contracts.invariant: Ordinary GC does not create Scheme rebuild debt for stable hashes. Deserialization NEED_REHASH still blocks direct indexed lookup until Scheme reconstructs. GC never executes user hash callbacks.
contracts.benefit: Semantic key/index agreement and no extra Scheme O(n) rebuild after every collection
contracts.cost: Existing explicit rebuild may allocate/call user hash. Same-table mutating reentrancy and simultaneous reconstruction are not proved by this cut.

contracts.route: gc-hash-table-resize flag retention; table-copy -> make-table-aux; serialize/deserialize flags
contracts.invariant: Ownership survives allocation, resize, copy and current-format roundtrip. Older serialized images without owner metadata and external raw flag writers remain unqualified.
contracts.benefit: Owner is a persistent native contract, not a GC-mode switch or an exception for GSC
contracts.cost: Additional serialization/FFI producer inventory and native tests required; no compatibility inference

contracts.cost: Full native and source-refinement gates; first target link is insufficient
